verdict.rationale: LanceDB documents table branching: isolated, writable forks of table history where experiments, backfills, and index rebuilds run "without disturbing production reads on main." A dedicated agent-experiment guide shows isolating work on a branch and promoting only the winner. This is genuine write isolation, not just a dry-run, but it is scoped to individual tables. Missing for 10: an environment- or database-level sandbox (e.g., separate sandbox projects or credentials), detailed documentation of isolation guarantees, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Fork isolated, writable lines of table history in LanceDB. Run experiments, backfills, and index rebuilds without disturbing production reads on main.
Use LanceDB branches to isolate agent-driven experiments from main, evaluate them on a fixed test set, and promote only the winner.
LanceDB supports branching to isolate experiments from the main table when working with agents.
